subject: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@datawave.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Marty O'Neill <marty.oneill@datawave.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're running a formal RFP bake-off next month to evaluate Redwood vs OrionAI and a couple of other vendors. Procurement has asked us to collect standardized cost/perf results under a 2-week controlled evaluation.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide a short-term credits package + trial extension so our engineers can run the same prompts and embedding workflows used in the RFP? Rough target workload: ~250k generation tokens, 5k embeddings, concurrent test up to 8 workers, 10k prompt calls/day peak.

We'd also like a proposed mutual action plan and a simple addendum that covers a one-time evaluation credit and a 30-45 day trial extension. We can share the dataset and metrics once you confirm.

cc: Marty (procurement) who will handle PO/terms.

Best,
Sara Jenkins
VP, Product
DataWave.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@datawave.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and for including the scope. We can absolutely support a side-by-side evaluation and want to make it as frictionless as possible.

Proposed eval package (one-time):
- 300,000 generation token credits
- 5,000 embedding credits
- 45-day trial extension on a dedicated eval project

I've attached a lightweight evaluation plan (eval-plan.pdf) with suggested runner scripts, model variants (including a lower-cost quantized variant for throughput runs), and a mutual action plan. Deal ID: HSP-87654 (tracking in HubSpot).

To move forward I need 3 quick items from you:
1) Confirm dataset size / approx token count for the seed set
2) Confirm target latency/SLO (p95 latency or tail requirement)
3) Contact for procurement so we can send the addendum

Once we have procurement contact, we can run the addendum through DocuSign and provision the credits immediately after.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@datawave.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline

Sara — quick technical notes from our side after reviewing the dataset outline you shared in the product call: 

- For generation tests: we recommend running 2 model variants (redwood-std-xx and redwood-lite-q4) to capture latency vs quality tradeoffs.
- For embeddings: batch size = 64 recommended; we can provide example batching scripts used in our bench harness.
- If you're testing concurrency up to 8 workers, let us know whether you prefer throughput-first (saturate GPUs) or latency-first (reserve smaller batches).

Also: please confirm whether the evaluation dataset contains any PII or regulated data — if yes we will route provisioning through Private project workflows (still fine, just need approvals).

Happy to jump on a 30-min tech sync next week.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline

Marcus — looping you in to approve a one-time promo credit for DataWave. Field asks: 300k gen tokens + 5k embeddings + 45-day extension.

Recommendation: classify this as a marketing/eval credit (no recurring discount), issue promo code DW-BAKEOFF-300K, cap usage at the credit amounts, and require a signed simple addendum (no changes to standard SLA). Attached are our cost estimate notes (redwood-credit-notes.xlsx).

Q: Can finance recognize this as a contra-revenue marketing expense? Also – any restrictions we should add for competitor parity language in the addendum? DataWave specifically called out that they're comparing against OrionAI and expect parity reporting.

Thx,
Steph

On Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 08:22 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sara — quick technical notes...
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP bake-off: request for evaluation credits and timeline

Steph / Jonas — approved. Conditions:
- One-time credits only; any excess billed at standard rates.
- Usage cap enforced per the attached DW-BAKEOFF promotion terms (we'll produce the addendum).
- No competitor-exclusivity or permanent parity clauses — we can provide a small paragraph allowing them to state they ran a comparative test but no claims about our competitive pricing beyond the eval period.

I'll route a short addendum through DocuSign (link below). Finance agrees to code this as a marketing credit.

DocuSign (addendum): https://www.docusign.com/drive/placeholder-ds-link

Marcus Lin
Finance, Redwood Inference
